actual_scope: Kappa-blocker KB3e (set level, no words): decide whether any 18-point set covers F2^7 (PR943 covering condition P + P = F2^7; every mask of F2^7 a pair-sum a + b of elements of the set). Delivered outcome=partial: the question is not decided (neither excluded nor constructed) but narrowed to an exact finite remainder. (1) The PR 2870 odd-coverage Fourier/Parseval squeeze is re-derived for the four counting-feasible splits (12,6),(11,7),(10,8),(9,9) with the deficit tracked per split: its opposite-parity hypothesis fails on all of them (18 is even) and the deficits are non-positive (e.g. (11,7) remainders 1166/798 vs allowed 21294; (9,9) 990/990 vs 36414). (2) A per-character profile system (parity, |rho_hat| <= E_o with rho_hat == E_o (mod 2), the even-half bound f_hat^2 + g_hat^2 <= s + t + 2P - 2^n, Parseval, exact attainable sums of squares of rho) excludes no 18-point split but PROVES that any (12,6) or (10,8) cover must have a vanishing character off the all-ones hyperplane (the no-vanishing sub-case is infeasible; for (12,6) it would force sum rho^2 = 46, unattainable). The same system reproduces PR 2870's (11,6) exclusion and PR 2773's (10,7) exclusion. (3) PR 2773's pair-representation rows extended to the four splits with the reproduced census floors leave 808 / 501 / 251 / 196 surviving rows ((e_ex, b_ex, c) lists exact; contingency-table pairing sums validated against the vendored engine). (4) Bounded seeded construction search: no 18-point cover found (direct k=18, 200 restarts, best 118/128; per-split structured searches best 118/118/118/117), with a k=20 non-vacuity control finding covers in 10/10 short runs. Every recorded predecessor anchor was reproduced before any new number (see ANCHOR-REPRO.json; both heavy census anchors recomputed in full by fresh empty-receipt walks). No word enumeration (the L=20 repeated-state word census is Nicholas Stone's concurrent claim); no kappa, supplier or selected-frontier change; the gap 20 <= f(7) <= 24 is unchanged.
